master_narrator.agency_handoff_prompt:
The storm had passed, but the static remained. It clung to the Enclave like a second skin.

Kenna walked the halls of the sleeping quarters, checking the bio-monitors. It was 0300 hours, yet half the family was awake. The air pressure had dropped too quickly, and the magnetic residue played havoc with the colony's circadian rhythms.

She found Silas scrubbing the floor panel outside the galley. His hands moved in rigid, mechanical circles. The planetary Schumann resonance anomalies had scrambled his pineal gland. The persistent electromagnetic flux mimicked high noon, suppressing his melatonin production and flooding his serotonin receptors with static.

"It is not clean," Silas muttered. He scrubbed the pristine metal harder. "The dust. It is everywhere."

He sought to scrub away an invisible threat. She needed to break the loop, administer the psychoactive Lyceum bryophytes, and initiate zero-dust flotation to decouple his nervous system from the magnetic variance. But the harsh chemical tang of the cleaning solvent stung her nose. A sharp spike of her own Aquarius detachment—a clinical urge to simply log his biometric telemetry and walk away—rose in her throat.

She held the rigging and high-altitude lifelines taut when the katabatic gales hit the exterior shielding. Here inside, she coaxed Silas off his hands and knees at 0300 hours with a promise of zero dust. She knelt beside him, placing a warm hand over his trembling fingers. He flinched, then froze.

"The floor is structurally sound, Silas," Kenna said. Her tone remained carefully modulated, a precise acoustic instrument designed to induce alpha brain waves. "The dust is negligible. You need REM sleep."

"I just want it to be clean," he whispered, a brittle edge to his voice.

"I know," Kenna said, her smile gentle. "If you're complaining and no one is laughing, you're complaining wrong. Come to the Lyceum. Elias has the sensory deprivation tank ready. Zero gravity. Zero dust. Just you and the void."

He stopped scrubbing. "Zero dust?"

"Absolute zero."

Silas lowered the brush, a long exhale leaving his lungs. Therefore, he stood up, leaning slightly on her shoulder as they walked down the humming corridor.

She led him to the isolation chamber. The dark water within sat perfectly still. It would conceal his physical form from harsh sensory inputs, consume the residual static through the suspended psychoactive moss, and defend his fragile neurochemistry against the ongoing geomagnetic storm.

Kenna watched him submerge, noting the immediate drop in his heart rate on the glass monitor. She picked up the intercom, dialing the observation deck. "Elias. The subject is stabilized. He is yours now. Keep the tank parameters locked."
